When Apple finally responded to the issue of rising memory and other component costs, its stance was notably tough. Some models saw price hikes of over fifty percent, while upgrades to memory and storage on certain configurations nearly doubled in price.

These higher prices are expected to persist for years, and may even become permanent pricing...

9to5Mac readers have long been skeptical about whether Apple would reduce prices once component shortages eased. Over two-thirds of respondents indicated that they expected these price increases to be permanent.

Subsequently, analyst reports noted that supply chain prices would not see significant improvement until at least 2028, and even if conditions eased by then, any reductions would be quite limited. The current high pricing policy appears set to last at least several years, and may never return to previous levels.

If this is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same frequency? Or would you reduce the quantity or frequency of your purchases? Alternatively, would you take other approaches, such as choosing more affordable models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a purchase?

Feel free to participate in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments section. The poll offers multiple options, allowing you to indicate several changes to your purchasing habits at once.
